notes: Second full sweep at db91c23: five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. No transcript has a Skill tool call or any SKILL.md text, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. In the scratch folder, mix format --check-formatted passes for haiku-1 and haiku-2 and fails for opus-1 (lines 25, 30, 84), sonnet-1 (lines 37, 88-89) and sonnet-2 (line 51); all five compile, with warnings only that Decimal is not loaded. Opus-1 also left check/check.exs (a Decimal stand-in and a smoke script) in its run folder after its rm was refused; that file is not graded.

Changed rule, now in the case's list and graded per run: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, the rule's first paragraph and the paragraph after its first example). Violating runs out of 5: one-step with 1 (opus-1 line 50, around parse_all/1 in build/1); else 1 (opus-1 lines 127-128, which rewrite Decimal.parse/1 and finite?/1 results into one error, the shape the previous sweep flagged in skill-sonnet-1); case nested in a with 0. The other four write no with (not exercised): haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 raise on bad input instead of returning tuples. For comparison, the previous sweep's baseline runs had the one-step shape in 3 of 5 (opus-1 line 57, sonnet-1 line 87, sonnet-2 line 35), not graded then because the rule was not in the case's list.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job", decided by its second table row: "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand". Hand-written per-key fold: 5 of 5. Per currency: opus-1 lines 66-67 (a for comprehension with reduce:), haiku-1 lines 53-56, sonnet-1 lines 63-64, sonnet-2 line 51; per customer: haiku-2 lines 44-46 with Map.get/Map.put at lines 63 and 78, sonnet-2 lines 34-42. The first check batch already read the per-currency Map.update fold as counting under this row. The previous sweep graded the same per-currency shape clean under the old text (its baseline-opus-1 lines 71-72, baseline-haiku-2 lines 57-60, baseline-sonnet-2 lines 105-106), so the move to violated for Opus and Sonnet reflects the new row; only haiku-2's Map.get then Map.put fold would also break the old text (row `Map.put(map, k, f.(Map.get(map, k)))`). Opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-1 group customers with Enum.group_by/2 and Map.new/2, the function the case's check line now names.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming (fetch sentence: "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`."; variable sentence: "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name."). Neither added sentence decides a verdict here: no run defines a lookup helper (haiku-2 calls the standard Map.fetch!/2), and no run names a variable data. Violating runs per sentence, out of 5: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0 (Reports.Orders as the prompt names it); boolean functions end in ? 0 (opus-1 finite?/1, haiku-1 completed?/1, sonnet-1 a completed? key); get/fetch 0; size/length 0 (not exercised); ignored values 0; domain variable names 1 (sonnet-2 line 64: latest(a, b), the line the previous sweep flagged in baseline-sonnet-1). acc, entry, id, rows, string, value and current are held to the earlier standard, which passed them and flagged only data and single letters.

Unchanged rule, new finding: "Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer" is decided by its first sentence and "When the body does more than one call or would need `&2`, write `fn` with named arguments." Sonnet-2 line 51 writes a capture whose body calls Map.update/4 and, through an inner fn, Decimal.add/2; because captures cannot nest, the one-call lambda inside is written as fn. The rule's form is fn totals -> Map.update(totals, currency, amount, &Decimal.add(&1, amount)) end. No earlier run in this case wrote that shape.

Other unchanged rules follow the earlier standard. Decimal.parse/1 catch-alls are listed under Match every expected shape (opus-1 line 128; sonnet-1 line 82, which raises instead of returning a tuple). Raising on malformed rows is listed under the raise rule (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Reading string keys inside the report code is listed under Read required keys and Parse external data (haiku-1, sonnet-2), as in the previous baseline-haiku-2. A public build/1 with an @doc lacking ## Examples is listed (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2), and so is one with no @doc at all (sonnet-1, sonnet-2). A two-step pipeline on one line is listed (sonnet-1 line 67), as in the previous skill-haiku-1, and format failures go under Before you finish. One new finding: sonnet-2's add_spend/2 selects the status and matches the fields in one head (line 49), so a completed row missing "amount" or "currency" falls through to the no-op clause (line 54). A probe with a stand-in Decimal confirmed that such a row counts toward top_customers but is left out of totals. It is listed under Match every expected shape, whose last paragraph says to select the type in one function and validate the fields in another.

baseline-sonnet-2.summary: Folds the raw string-keyed rows into per-customer summaries with Enum.reduce and Map.update, with Decimal totals and DateTime.compare/2, and counts completed orders with frequencies_by. It breaks the Enum/Map rule (per-key folds), Naming (latest(a, b)) and the captures rule (a two-call capture wrapping an fn). Outside the list, it silently drops completed rows missing amount or currency from the totals, reads required keys with order["key"] without parsing at the boundary, raises on malformed input, gives build/1 no @doc, and fails mix format. It read no skill files.
